name: The chariot simile of Kaṭha Upaniṣad 1.3

definitions.definition: The self is the lord of the chariot, the body the chariot, the intellect (buddhi) the charioteer, the mind (manas) the reins, the senses (indriya) the horses and the objects (viṣaya) their roads (1.3.3-4). With an unyoked mind the senses are unruly like bad horses and one goes to saṃsāra; with a yoked mind they are obedient like good horses and one reaches the highest place of Viṣṇu, from which there is no rebirth (1.3.5-9).

name: The ascending order beyond the senses (Kaṭha 1.3.10-11)

definitions.definition: Above the senses are the objects, above them the mind, above it the intellect, above it the great self (mahān ātmā), above it the unmanifest (avyakta), above it the person (puruṣa); nothing is higher than the person, who is the limit and the highest goal.
